changelog:
- Roll back partially initialized sync sessions immediately when startup fails or is cancelled
- Dispose unowned FFmpeg streams and restore saved lights before waiting for playback stop
- Add regression coverage for startup restoration, area deactivation, ownership, and diagnostics
- Stop sync after repeated DTLS send failures instead of leaving lights frozen
- Restore saved light states and deactivate the entertainment area after send-failure exits
- Add regression coverage for bounded stream failure cleanup and error reporting
- Add automatic terminal cleanup when FFmpeg reaches EOF or the frame stream fails
- Restore saved light states and deactivate the entertainment area after terminal sync-loop exits
- Add regression coverage for EOF cleanup, failure cleanup, runtime ownership, and error preservation
- Add per-user sync opt-out controls for multi-user Jellyfin deployments
- Allow disabled user mappings to omit bridge credentials while preserving the default bridge for unmapped users
- Enforce per-user sync preferences before validation, FFmpeg startup, or Hue network calls
- Add regression coverage for disabled mappings, defaults, and runtime startup suppression
- Add a protected Stop Current Sync control that restores lights while playback continues
- Suppress automatic sync restarts for the manually stopped playback session until playback ends
- Report whether an administrator can stop the current sync session in runtime status
- Add lifecycle regression coverage for manual stop, stale stop notifications, and session suppression
- Add an optional non-destructive DTLS stream probe to Test Connection
- Verify the Hue Client Key and report whether a probe packet was written
- Add sanitized stream-probe result fields and regression coverage
- Add live runtime status and sanitized playback diagnostics to the API and configuration UI
- Show active bridge/area, frame count, sync duration, and FFmpeg/DTLS health while playback is running
- Add lifecycle regression coverage without exposing Hue credentials
- Add non-destructive bridge connection testing to the API and configuration UI
- Verify selected entertainment areas contain controllable channels
- Add explicit edit and cancel controls for per-user bridge mappings
- Load entertainment areas through a body-based API so Hue app keys are not sent in URLs
- Keep the legacy GET area endpoint available for existing clients
- Add authenticated bridge discovery to the configuration API and UI
- Add one-click discovery for default and per-user bridge mappings
- Keep plugin JSON and encoding dependencies on the .NET 8 servicing line
- Pin vulnerable legacy transitive framework packages to safe compatible versions
- Use the Hue bridge HTTPS API for link-button registration on current firmware
- Scope local certificate handling to private bridge addresses
- Require bridge targets to be private/local addresses or .local mDNS names
- Hardened playback lifecycle cleanup across stop, pause, resume, and shutdown events
- Added transient Hue bridge HTTP retries and malformed-response handling
- Improved FFmpeg and DTLS process ownership and reconnect safety
- Added validation for per-user bridge mappings and stream packet inputs
- Updated release packaging and documentation
description: Synchronize Philips Hue lights with your media playback in real-time.
name: Philips Hue Sync
overview: Adds support for real-time lighting synchronization with Philips Hue Entertainment Areas using the streaming DTLS API. Features cinema mode, scene restoration, per-user bridge mappings, advanced color processing, and auto-reconnection.
